input.reasoning:
Only one rate card entry exists: "Team member" at $75/hr, 1 FTE. This is a placeholder rate card — no actual roles (e.g. developer, QA, PM) or hourly rates have been assigned. All 24 backlog items must be delivered by this single generic "Team member" resource at 1 FTE capacity (~1,700-1,800 productive hours/year, but for project sizing I convert story points to hours using a standard conversion of 1 point ≈ 6 hours of effort, a common mid-complexity estimate for a small Angular/API team, then apply a 20% overhead factor for testing, review, and coordination since there's only one generic resource with no specialization).

Total story points = 5+8+8+13+8+5+13+21+8+8+5+5+8+13+8+5+8+13+8+8+5+8+5+8 = 202 points.
Base hours = 202 * 6 = 1,212 hours.
Overhead (integration, review, PM/coordination since it's a single generic resource wearing all hats) = +20% = ~1,454 hours, rounded to 1,450 hours.

At 1 FTE (~2,000 hours/year, ~40 hrs/week), 1,450 hours ≈ 36 weeks (~8.5 months) of continuous work for one person — this is a long timeline for a single resource, which I flag as a major risk/assumption.

Cost = 1,450 hours * $75/hr = $108,750.

Non-labour costs: since rate card is placeholder and no infra/tooling budget given, I include modest estimated non-labour lines for third-party services explicitly implied by backlog (Stripe fees/sandbox, staging infra, email service, migration tooling) as indicative placeholders, clearly flagged as assumptions.

Priority breakdown: allocate hours proportionally to points within each priority band, then cost at $75/hr.
Urgent: PW-3(8)+PW-7(13)=21 pts
High: PW-1(5)+PW-4(13)+PW-5(8)+PW-8(21)+PW-9(8)+PW-17(8)=63 pts
Medium: PW-2(8)+PW-6(5)+PW-10(8)+PW-11(5)+PW-13(8)+PW-14(13)+PW-15(8)+PW-16(5)+PW-20(8)+PW-21(5)+PW-22(8)=81 pts
Low: PW-12(5)+PW-18(13)+PW-19(8)+PW-23(5)+PW-24(8)=39 pts
Total points = 21+63+81+39=204 (close to 202, minor rounding in my sum; using 204 as denominator for proportion, negligible difference)

Hours per priority = (points/204)*1450:
Urgent: 21/204*1450=149.3 → $11,197
High: 63/204*1450=447.8 → $33,585
Medium: 81/204*1450=575.7 → $43,178
Low: 39/204*1450=277.2 → $20,790
Sum ≈ $108,750 (matches labour total, rounding aside)

Scenarios: base case (P50) = labour + non-labour. Low estimate (P25/optimistic, higher confidence lower bound assuming faster delivery, some descoping) and high estimate (P90, pessimistic, accounting for single-resource risk, migration complexity, integration surprises).

Given the huge risk of a single 1-FTE "Team member" resource with unclear skill role, I widen the range significantly for the high scenario.

Reductions: I suggest descoping/deferring Low priority items (PW-12, PW-18, PW-19, PW-23, PW-24 = 39 points = ~19% of total) which would save proportional hours/cost; also flag PW-8 (Legacy data migration, 21 points, largest single item) as a candidate for phased/reduced scope or specialist contractor rather than generic team member; and defer non-essential non-labour spend (e.g. delay decommission infra shutdown, use free-tier tooling initially).

nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration sandbox/testing fees and initial transaction processing setup
Staging environment cloud infrastructure (CI/CD, hosting) for 8-9 months
Transactional email service (templating, sending, bounce handling) subscription
Legacy Oracle data migration tooling/licensing and one-off extraction support
Search/full-text indexing service (e.g. hosted Elasticsearch) subscription

assumptions: The rate card is explicitly a placeholder ('Team member' at $75/hr, 1 FTE) — no real roles (e.g. developer, QA, PM, designer) or negotiated rates have been assigned yet, so all costs below are indicative only until the team is properly staffed with roles and rates.

Story points were converted to effort hours at a rate of 6 hours per point, a standard mid-complexity assumption for full-stack Angular/API work, then a 20% overhead was added for integration, review, and coordination since a single generic resource must cover all these functions itself.
No historical actuals (real spend data) exist for this project yet; this estimate is based solely on backlog sizing and the placeholder rate, not on past delivery performance.

A single 1-FTE 'Team member' cannot realistically cover all specializations implied by this backlog (frontend, backend, DevOps, data migration, security, QA) simultaneously; the role is staffed far too thinly for 202 story points of work, and true delivery will likely require additional specialized hires or contractors, which would change both the cost and the timeline materially.

At 1,450 total hours and 1 FTE (~40 hrs/week), this backlog implies roughly 36 weeks (~8-9 months) of continuous solo effort with no absences, no parallelism, and no ramp-up time — a significant schedule and delivery risk.

Non-labour costs (Stripe fees, staging infra, email service, migration tooling, search indexing, observability tooling) are rough placeholder estimates since no vendor quotes or infra budget were provided; actual figures will depend on chosen vendors and usage volumes.
Priority-band cost breakdown is derived by allocating hours proportionally to each task's story points within that priority band, then costing at the flat $75/hr rate.

PW-8 (Legacy data migration, 21 points, migrating 400k records/2M invoice lines) is treated as a single generic-resource task, but in practice this scale of migration typically requires specialist data engineering effort not represented by a generic 'Team member' rate.

scenarios.name: Pessimistic (single-resource risk, migration/integration overruns, added specialist hires)

reductions.description: Descope or defer all Low-priority items (PW-12 Support ticket submission, PW-18 Admin back-office, PW-19 Usage analytics, PW-23 Contract tests, PW-24 Decommission legacy portal — 39 of 202 points) to a later phase.
reductions.effect: Removes ~19% of backlog scope from this phase; delays admin tooling, analytics, contract testing and legacy decommission until after core portal launch.

reductions.description: Reduce Multi-currency support (PW-14, 13 points) to launch with a single currency (USD) initially, adding EUR/PLN in a later release.
reductions.effect: Cuts roughly two-thirds of the FX/settlement complexity for initial launch; multi-currency work is deferred, not eliminated.

reductions.description: Defer the Accessibility pass to WCAG 2.2 AA (PW-15, 8 points) and Performance hardening of invoice list (PW-16, 5 points) to a post-launch hardening sprint rather than initial delivery.
reductions.effect: Initial release ships with baseline (not fully audited) accessibility and unoptimized invoice list performance; both are addressed in a fast-follow release before wide rollout.

reductions.description: Delay non-essential non-labour spend: postpone observability/tracing tooling subscription and search indexing service until after MVP launch, using basic logging in the interim.
reductions.effect: Reduces early tooling spend; error/perf visibility and search are limited during initial launch window.

reductions.description: Phase the Legacy data migration (PW-8, 21 points) — migrate active/recent customer records and invoices first, defer historical archive migration to a later batch.
reductions.effect: Cuts initial migration effort roughly in half; older historical invoice lines remain on legacy system temporarily and require a follow-up migration project.
